outcomes.text: Choose an auxiliary for an ordinary negative or question, including when do is needed.
Build an auxiliary chain in order and select the verb form required at each step.
Explain selected differences in tense, aspect and modal interpretation in context.

key_terms.definition: A verb that can fill special grammatical roles, such as carrying negation or appearing before the subject in a question.
The use of auxiliary do when a construction needs an auxiliary and the clause lacks a suitable one.
The uninflected verb form used after modal auxiliaries and supportive do, as in check.
A verb form used in constructions such as has checked, was checked or is checking.
A tense choice in an embedded report that takes the original occasion of speaking as a reference point.

options.feedback: Did carries past tense, so test takes the plain form.
Did carries past tense, so test takes the plain form.

opening.prompt: Which question asks whether Nina tested the valve?

options.feedback: Perfect have selects a past participle. Left is the past participle of leave.
Perfect have selects a past participle. Left is the past participle of leave.

opening.prompt: What follows perfect have in “The crew might have ___”?

options.text: Nina has inspected it twice since nine.
options.feedback: The simple past fits the dated event. Since nine can instead open a period continuing to the present.

options.text: Nina inspected it at nine yesterday.
options.feedback: The simple past fits the dated event. Since nine can instead open a period continuing to the present.

options.text: Nina has inspected it at nine yesterday.
options.feedback: The simple past fits the dated event. Since nine can instead open a period continuing to the present.

opening.prompt: Which line places an event at a definite finished past time?

options.feedback: Who fills the subject slot. What and when ask about other parts.
Who fills the subject slot. What and when ask about other parts.

options.text: When did Nina check the lock?
options.feedback: Who fills the subject slot. What and when ask about other parts.

opening.prompt: Which one is an ordinary question about the subject?

options.feedback: Has selects been for the perfect. Progressive been then selects testing.
Has selects been for the perfect. Progressive been then selects testing.

options.text: The crew has been testing it.
options.feedback: Has selects been for the perfect. Progressive been then selects testing.

opening.prompt: Which wording has both perfect and progressive aspect?

options.feedback: Only the first auxiliary moves before the subject.
Only the first auxiliary moves before the subject.

options.text: Did the alarm might have sounded?
options.feedback: Only the first auxiliary moves before the subject.

closing.prompt: How do you ask about a definite possibility in “The alarm might have sounded”?

options.text: The key may have been copying.
options.feedback: May takes plain have, have takes been, and passive been takes copied.

options.text: The key may have been copied.
options.feedback: May takes plain have, have takes been, and passive been takes copied.

options.text: The key may has been copied.
options.feedback: May takes plain have, have takes been, and passive been takes copied.

closing.prompt: Which report combines a modal with a perfect passive?

options.text: Lea said she is leaving before Jo returns.
options.feedback: Was and returned both shift to the past viewpoint of the original utterance.

options.text: Lea said she was leaving before Jo returns.
options.feedback: Was and returned both shift to the past viewpoint of the original utterance.

options.text: Lea said she was leaving before Jo returned.
options.feedback: Was and returned both shift to the past viewpoint of the original utterance.

closing.prompt: Lea said, “I’m leaving before Jo returns.” Which report backshifts both embedded present tenses?

options.feedback: The negative imperative uses plain supportive do, even with be.
The negative imperative uses plain supportive do, even with be.
The negative imperative uses plain supportive do, even with be.

closing.prompt: Which is an ordinary direct negative instruction?

options.feedback: The progressive presents the leaking as ongoing. The composition statements describe stable states.

options.text: The tank consists of two chambers.
options.feedback: The progressive presents the leaking as ongoing. The composition statements describe stable states.

closing.prompt: Which wording presents an activity in progress?
